title: An Open Source Technology Platform to Manufacture Hydrogel-Based 3D Culture Models in an Automated and Standardized Fashion
protocol: Set up the computer environment.
Open a terminal window from the taskbar or application menu.
Update the system’s package list using sudo apt-get update.
Upgrade all the installed packages using sudo apt-get dist-upgrade.
Restart the Raspberry Pi.
Clone the GitHub repository https://github.com/SebastianEggert/OpenWorkstation.
Open the downloaded folder containing the files for the experiment.
Navigate to the ‘publication-JoVE’ folder if the entire repository was cloned.
Place the workstation in a biological safety cabinet.
Install pipettes on the workstation.
Select the pipette size based on the experimental setup.
Choose a pipette with a volume range that accommodates the highest volume required, such as M1000E for volumes greater than 1 mL.
Calculate the required mass of GelMA based on the desired final stock concentration and volume.
Weigh the calculated amount of lyophilized GelMA and add it into a 50 mL reaction tube.
Add phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the weighed GelMA in the reaction tube.
Mix GelMA by soaking into the solvent at 4 °C overnight or by heating to 60 °C for 6 h in a water bath.
Calculate the required mass of LAP based on the desired final stock concentration and volume.
Weigh the calculated amount of LAP and add it into a 15 mL reaction tube.
Add PBS to the weighed LAP in the reaction tube.
Wrap the tube in aluminum foil to prevent photo-induced decomposition.
Place the reaction tube in a water bath at 37 °C for 2 h or until fully dissolved LAP.
Calculate required amount of alginate based on desired final stock concentration and volume using the equation.
Weigh the required mass of alginate, add it into a 50 mL reaction tube, and add PBS.
Place the alginate mix into a water bath at 37 °C for 4 h.
Fill 5 mL of alginate into 5 mL reaction tubes.
Fill 5 mL of glycerol in 5 mL reaction tubes.
Prepare a 10 mg/mL stock solution of Orange G in a 50 mL reaction tube.
Dilute Orange G stock solution to a 1 mg/mL working solution in a 50 mL reaction tube.
Transfer working solution to appropriate flasks/tubes for the experimental setup.
Fill 5 mL of the 1 mg/mL Orange G working solution in 5 mL reaction tubes.
Open the protocol designer application by running ‘ProtocolDesignApp.html’.
Enter protocol name (e.g., double-network-hydrogels) on setup page.
Click ‘Continue’ to confirm protocol name and proceed to the next step.
Select ‘3x4 Heating Block’ from drop-down menu for input tray definition.
Select ‘Gel 1’ from drop-down menu, enter name ‘GelMA’, enter stock-concentration ‘20%’, set ‘Number of Samples’ to ‘3’ to fill one column.
Click ‘+add’ to save entries.
Select ‘Gel 2’ from drop-down menu, enter name: ‘Alginate’, enter stock-concentration ‘4%’, set ‘Number of Samples’ to ‘3’ to fill one column.
Click ‘+add’ to save entries.
Select ‘Photoinitiator’ from drop-down menu, enter name: ‘LAP’, enter stock-concentration ‘3%’, set ‘Number of Samples’ to ‘3’ to fill one column.
Click ‘+add’ to save entries.
Select ‘Diluent 1’ from drop-down menu, enter name: ‘PBS’, set ‘Number of Samples’ to ‘3’ to fill one column.
Click ‘+add’ to save entries.
Define crosslinking parameters by checking ‘Photo crosslinking’.
Type the time in seconds, ‘30’, for photo crosslinking.
Type the intensity W/m² with ‘2’ for photo crosslinking.
Finish input setup by clicking ‘CONTINUE’.
Define output tray setup by selecting ’96 well plate’ from the drop-down menu for well plate type.
Click on ‘Group1’ to define outputs and create a group of samples.
Specify output composition by entering GelMA concentration as ‘5’.
Enter Alginate concentration as ‘2’.
Enter LAP concentration as ‘0.15’.
Set Total Volume to ‘60’.
Check the box to apply advanced mixing protocol.
Specify number of samples by entering the number of samples into the field ‘Number of Samples’: ‘96’.
Select tray position on the deck layout and prepare the platform accordingly.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT A1’ and select ‘Empty_Cell’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT A2’ and select ‘Trash_Cell’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT B1’ and select ‘Tips_Cell_100µL’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT B2’ and select ‘Tips_Cell_1000µL’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT C1’ and select ‘Input_Cell’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT C2’ and select ‘Empty_Cell’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT D1’ and select ‘Mixing_Cell’ from drop-down menu.
Check checkmark in field ‘SLOT D2’ and select ‘Output_Cell’ from drop-down menu.

Define type and characteristics of first pipette (M100E) by checking ’Pipette Left’, selecting ‘10-100µL positive displacement’ from drop-down menu and setting aspirating speed = ‘600’, dispensing speed = ‘800’.

Define type and characteristics of second pipette (M1000E) by checking ’Pipette Right’, selecting ‘100-1000µL positive displacement’ from drop-down menu and setting aspirating speed = ‘800’, dispensing speed = ‘1200’.
Navigate to the protocol folder.
Open the calibration terminal.
Execute the file ‘calibrate.py’ in a terminal window.
Select movement increments for plunger x, y, z movement using the numeric keypad.
Press keyboard shortcut P to select pipette size.
Press keyboard shortcut V to enter the plunger calibration mode.

Calibrate the following plunger positions: T–Top = rest position; B–Bottom = plunger is pushed until resistance is met; P–Pick-up = plunger is pushed to a position where a piston tip can be attached; E–Eject = plunger is pushed until an attached tip is ejected.
Vary plunger positions using the upwards and downwards arrows on the keyboard.
Save the final position using S on the keyboard.
Leave the pipette plunger calibration mode by pressing keyboard shortcut V.
Calibrate container position relative to the pipette tip.
Press keyboard shortcut P to select pipette type.
Ensure a tip is connected to the selected pipette.
Press keyboard shortcut C to select container type.
Calibrate to the ‘A1’ well position at the bottom for well plates.
Calibrate to the ‘A1’ position for tip racks.
Choose a point for ejecting tips into the trash.
Save each position with keyboard shortcut S.
Repeat steps for all containers listed under ‘C’ for the selected pipette type.
Repeat 5.3.1−5.3.5 for the second pipette type.
Close the calibration script.
Position trash container on the deck.
Position tip racks on the deck.
Position input tray on the deck.
Position mixing tray on the deck.
Position output tray on the deck.
Calibrate pipettes and instruments as defined in section 5.
Switch temperature dock ON if required.
Select temperature for input reagents according to setup.
Place tubes with input reagents in aluminum blocks on the temperature docks.
Wait until input reagents have reached the desired temperature.
Remove the well plate from workstation and transport it to a spectrophotometer.
Read absorbance with a spectrophotometer at 450 nm for each sample twice.
Export and save absorbance readings.
Copy absorbance readings into the ‘raw data’ sheet.
Ensure that all cell references are correctly defined in all tables.
Click on the ‘analysis’ sheet for information on average values.
Determine standard deviation values from the analysis sheet.
Calculate coefficient of variance (CV) values using the analysis sheet.
